assertions.evidence: @TableTest(""" Scenario | Items | Shipment count?" appears in all 5 test methods

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules.
assertions.evidence: Five separate methods: partitionsByFulfillmentType, partitionsByDeliveryAddress, separatesImmediateFromDelayedItems, minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses, coLocatesCompanionProducts

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Each table has 4-7 focused rows; e.g., fulfillment has 4 rows, delivery address has 4 rows, none mixing unrelated scenarios

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items with different fulfillment types (store pickup vs home delivery) cannot share a shipment.
assertions.evidence: partitionsByFulfillmentType() method with scenario 'One DELIVERY one PICKUP' → 2 shipments

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items going to different addresses must be in separate shipments.
assertions.evidence: partitionsByDeliveryAddress() method with scenario 'Different addresses' → 2 shipments

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — in-stock items ship immediately, backordered/pre-ordered items ship when available.
assertions.evidence: separatesImmediateFromDelayedItems() method showing IN_STOCK vs BACKORDERED in 'Immediate items?' and 'Delayed items?' columns

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation (minimising shipments) is represented as its own @TableTest — choosing which warehouses to ship from to minimise total shipment count.
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses() method with scenario 'Optimal 2 beats naive 3'

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest — paired items (e.g. camera body and lens) should ship together from the same location when possible.
assertions.evidence: coLocatesCompanionProducts() method with 'Together?' output column and scenarios like 'Both companions at one warehouse'

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods. All outputs of the same concern belong together.
assertions.evidence: partitionsByFulfillmentType has 'Shipment count?' and 'Fulfillment types?' in same @TableTest; separatesImmediateFromDelayedItems has 'Immediate items?' and 'Delayed items?' together

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation table uses scalar quantity columns (e.g. 'Qty ordered') not item lists, when product identity doesn't matter for the logic.
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses uses simple product identifiers [a,b,c] with implicit qty 1; comment states 'one unit each'

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: 'Scenario' appears as the leftmost column in all five @TableTest tables

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Shipments?', 'Groups?')
assertions.evidence: Multiple output columns end with '?': 'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Immediate items?', 'Delayed items?', 'Together?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Consolidate: two beats three', 'Everything at one warehouse') — not 'Test case 2'.
assertions.evidence: Scenarios like 'Optimal 2 beats naive 3', 'Both companions at one warehouse', 'In-stock with backordered' describe conditions

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language (e.g. 'Shipments?' not 'Result?', 'Warehouse stock' not 'inventory_map'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: Columns like 'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Warehouse stock', 'Together?' use business terminology

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: All five test methods contain only setup, method calls, and assertions; no control flow statements

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All five methods follow @DisplayName → @Description → @TableTest order consistently

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName annotations: 'Partition by fulfillment type', 'Choose warehouses to minimise shipment count'

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description annotations use triple-quoted text blocks: @Description("""...""")
